mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has a negative linear relationship with S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, as lower rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations through accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction of HOUST and RSAFS declining together fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive forward returns over the next 60 days as strong supply conditions support corporate profitability and economic expansion.
failure_condition: In the high industrial growth regime (INDPRO > 105), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) has a positive linear relationship with S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, as stronger labor markets support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over a 3-month period signals rising inflation pressures, which typically lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a severe economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction of HOUST and GDPC1 declining together fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong retail sales (RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive forward returns over the next 5 days as robust consumer spending supports corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: In the strong consumer spending regime (RSAFS > 350,000), the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
